en: I bow to Him who is the cause of joy for Prahlāda, who possesses a multitude of all virtues, who is pure existence, consciousness, and bliss;
who bears forms both gentle and fierce, who is eternally fearless, and who holds the discus, the conch, and Lakṣmī;
who is capable of destroying sins, and who is worshipped by Brahmā, Śiva, Garuḍa, Indra, and the other gods.
I bow to Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha, whose stainless eye shines as it pierces the chest of the Rākṣasa. 1.

I bow to the glorious one whose lotus feet are worshipped by the Lord of Serpents, who rests upon the hoods of the serpent-king; whose inner heart is intensely thrilled with love as he holds the earth-goddess on his left lap with cupped hands; whose virtues transcend all limits; and whose hands are raised in gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, while holding the conch, discus, and the excellent golden mace—the source of desire and other powers.
O mind, remember this stainless form of the Boar, which is worthy of praise through the Sāman hymns! 2.

Salutations to Hari, who has the hue of a blue lotus, who wears a forest garland, who possesses a mass of shimmering ornaments reaching to his ears, and who is the protector of the multitude of his own devotees. 3.

O source of the prosperity of all the gods, I suspect that you have taken up this nurse—who is a vessel of auspicious qualities—to nourish and abandon this one who is apprehensive regarding his remaining faults. 4.
Salutations be to Hari, the mountain of logic, the conqueror of enemies, the teacher of all, the wish-fulfilling tree for those who know the supreme reality. 5.
Thus ends the Varāhapañcaka composed by the venerable ascetic Vādirāja.
